ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left end of the structure is H3C–C≡C–, and this alkyne bond continues to connect to a central C=C double bond. The carbon on the left side of the central double bond is also connected down to the left to a –CH2CH2CH3 propyl branch; the carbon on the right side of the central double bond is connected upward to CH3 and down to the right to –CH2CH2CH3. Reasoning: Select the main chain according to the specified method, from the left-end CH3 through C≡C into the central C=C, then extending along the right-side propyl group, obtaining an 8-carbon main chain. When numbered from the left end, the triple bond is at C2, and the double bond is at C4. The substituents not included in the main chain are propyl at C4 and methyl at C5. Combining them gives the name 5-methyl-4-propyl-4-octene-2-acetylene; the modern equivalent writing is 5-methyl-4-propyloct-4-en-2-yne.

method.method_draft: Trace the parent chain from the left CH3 through C≡C into the central C=C and then along the right-hand propyl group, giving an 8-carbon parent chain. Number from the left CH3 end so the triple bond is at C2 and the double bond is at C4. Identify the remaining branches: a propyl substituent on C4 and a methyl substituent on C5. Combine these to obtain the name in the expected style: 5-methyl-4-propyl-4-octene-2-acetylene, equivalent to 5-methyl-4-propyloct-4-en-2-yne.

method.method_draft: Rewrite the pictured molecule as the condensed formula CH3–C≡C–C(CH2CH2CH3)=C(CH3)(CH2CH2CH3). Compare candidate 8-carbon parent paths: the path through the ethynyl side and the right propyl side includes both C≡C and C=C, whereas a path through the two propyl groups would omit the triple bond, so choose the former. Number from the alkynyl methyl end to place the alkyne at 2 and alkene at 4. The unused left propyl branch is at C4 and the unused methyl branch is at C5, giving 5-methyl-4-propyl-4-octene-2-acetylene.
